ACIAR Monograph 143, published by the Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research (ACIAR) in partnership with NSW Department of Primary Industries, the Cambodian Agricultural Research and Development Institute (CARDI), Murdoch University, University of Canberra, and MAFF, under ACIAR Project ASEM/2000/109. text:
This source recommends several ways to build soil nitrogen and reduce fertilizer costs using legumes as part of a corn rotation or intercrop:
- Rotating or relay-cropping corn with legume species -- for example mungbean planted in the early wet season and soybean planted in the main wet season -- allows nitrogen-fixing root-nodule bacteria associated with the legume to add nitrogen to the topsoil, reducing the fertilizer nitrogen needed by a following corn crop.
- Where a green-manure or cover crop (particularly a legume) is grown ahead of corn and incorporated into the soil, this also adds nitrogen and organic matter that benefits the following corn crop.

These practices are presented as complementary to, not a replacement for, careful mineral fertilizer management, but they can meaningfully reduce the amount of purchased nitrogen fertilizer needed.
